description: Source-range document-invariant contract (accept/reject parity, NOT the numeric formula). A media clip is valid only when sourceInUs >= 0, sourceOutUs > sourceInUs, and timelineDurationUs == roundHalfUp((sourceOutUs - sourceInUs) / speed.rate). Consumed by packages/timeline-schema/tests/invariants.test.ts (zod validateTimelineDoc) and backend/tests/VideoEdit.UnitTests/SourceRangeParityTests.cs (ExportCompiler.Validate). This closes one family of the document-invariant parity gap in docs/backlog.md (the class that produced C1): the half-up rounding of the duration formula is already vector-covered by time-vectors.json 'duration', but whether a whole document is ACCEPTED or REJECTED on this rule was measured in only one language. Every timelineDurationUs here is chosen to sit on the 30fps project frame grid so the C# referee (which checks the frame grid before the source range) does not short-circuit; the invalid cases keep a grid-valid duration and violate ONLY the source-range rule, isolating it. The half-up boundary itself cannot be shown grid-aligned (a .5 rounds to +1us, off-grid) and stays in time-vectors.json.
